paragraphs: Haqqiddush ben bayyom ben ballayla eno ella bimqom seuda mammash, shenneemar: "veqarata leshabbat oneg", vedareshu rz"l: bimqom oneg seudat shabbat, sham tihyeh qeriat haqqiddush. veal ken - la mibbaaya sheim qiddesh velo saad acharayv, shello yatza y"ch qiddush, ella gam im qiddesh bebayit zeh veakal bebayit acher, ben shehaya dato techilla leekol babbayit haacher, ben shehaya dato leekol babbayit sheqqiddesh bo veaach"k nimlak leekol babbayit haacher - lo yatza y"ch, vetzarik lachazor uleqaddesh qodem sheyyokal babbayit haacher. veyesh omerim, sheim bishat akilato babbayit haacher yakol lirot mishsham maqom sheqqiddesh bo apillu derek challon vaapillu miqtzato bilbad - chashibi shette meqomot ellu kemaqom echad leinyan qiddush veen tzarik lachazor uleqaddesh; veen lismok lekattechilla al sebara zo, laken yizzaher shello yabi atzmo lide kak. ubishat haddechaq shehutzrak lekak behekreach veeno yakol leqaddesh babbayit haacher, yesh lismok al sebarat hammeqillim beroeh et meqomo apillu mibbayit lebayit.

clarification.explanation: Kiddush, whether by day or night, must be recited in the place where the Sabbath meal is actually eaten, as it is said, "and you shall call the Sabbath a delight," and the Sages expounded that Kiddush must be recited where the delight of the meal is. Therefore, not only does one who recites Kiddush and does not eat afterward fail to fulfill his obligation, but even one who recites Kiddush in one house and goes to eat in another fails to fulfill it — and it makes no difference whether he planned in advance to eat in the other house or changed his mind afterward. In such a case he must recite Kiddush again before eating. Some say that if, while eating in the other house, he can see from there the place where he recited Kiddush, even through a window and even only part of it, the two places are considered one, and he need not recite Kiddush again. One should not rely on this leniency as the primary practice and should be careful not to get into such a situation; but in a case of great difficulty where there is no choice, one may rely on the lenient opinion that seeing one's place, even from house to house, suffices.
takeaways: Kiddush must be recited where the meal is eaten
If one recited Kiddush in one house and ate in another, he must recite Kiddush again
In a time of pressing need, one may rely on the opinion that seeing the place of Kiddush, even through a window, suffices

paragraphs: Shene chadarim bebayit echad, veqiddesh becheder zeh veokel bacheder hashsheni, o sheqqiddesh beara veokel beagra - im lo haya dato lekak veeno roeh et meqomo, lo yatza y"ch qiddush. veim haya dato lekak, "p sheeno roeh et meqomo en tzarik lachazor uleqaddesh kevan shehaya bebayit echad; mihu, im kol zeh, lekattechilla lo yaaseh ken. veim mukrach leekol bammaqom hashsheni, yizzaher leekol bemaqom sheqqiddesh bo kazzayit, veaach"k yokal bammaqom hashsheni. upoh irenu bagdad shekicha dabar zeh etzel hannashim, sheen darkam leekol al hashshulchan im haanashim "p sheen sham orechim zarim, ella darkam lishmoa qadosh becheder hashshulchan min bh"b, veaach"k holekim lecheder acher veokelin. veim hayu roim bacheder et meqom haqqiddush, vaapillu miqtzato – hecherashnu; ak da aqa, sheeno nireh meqom haqqiddush kelal. vezeh yimmatze al harob bebattim haggedolim shel haashirim; al ken yizzaharu leekol kazzayit bimqom haqqiddush veyeleku lecheder acher leekol sham.

clarification.explanation: If there are two rooms in the same house, and he recited Kiddush in one room and wants to eat in the second room, or he recited Kiddush downstairs and wants to eat upstairs — if he did not plan this in advance and cannot see the place of Kiddush, he has not fulfilled his obligation. But if he planned this in advance, even though he cannot see the place of Kiddush, he need not recite Kiddush again, since the two rooms are in the same house. Nevertheless, one should not act this way as the primary practice, and if he is compelled to eat in the second room he should be careful to first eat an olive's-worth of food in the place where he recited Kiddush, and only afterward go to eat in the second room. In Baghdad this is common among women, who are not accustomed to sit and eat with the men but hear Kiddush in the dining room from the master of the house and go to eat in another room. If they can see the place of Kiddush from there, there is no problem, but usually in the large houses they cannot see it, and therefore they should be careful to eat an olive's-worth in the place of Kiddush before going to eat in another room.
takeaways: Two rooms in the same house — if planned in advance, one need not recite Kiddush again, but this should not be done as the primary practice
The practical advice: eat an olive's-worth in the place of Kiddush, then move to another room
This ruling is especially relevant to women who are accustomed to eat in a separate room

paragraphs: Apillu becheder echad, im qiddesh bezavit zo al daat leekol sham, venimlak leekol bezavit sheniyya, lo yeaseh ken lekattechilla, "g demera"n za"l pasaq keharamba"m veharo"sh za"l deshare, k"z hari"p za"l udeimmeh choleqin. vekatebu haacharonim za"l degam mera"n za"l yodeh dilkattechilla la arik lemebad haki; laken, gam bazeh yaaseh kak, leekol kazzayit techilla bezavit sheqqiddesh bah veaach"k yipneh lezavit acheret.

clarification.explanation: Even within one room, if he recited Kiddush in one corner with the intention of eating there, and afterward changed his mind and wanted to eat in another corner — he should not do so as the primary practice. Although Maran ruled leniently on this, following the opinion of the Rambam and the Rosh, the Rif and his followers disagree, and the later authorities wrote that even Maran would agree that as the primary practice it is not proper to act this way. Therefore here too the correct way is to first eat an olive's-worth in the corner where he recited Kiddush, and only afterward move to the other corner.
takeaways: Even moving from corner to corner within the same room is not proper as the primary practice
Even the lenient opinions agree that as the primary practice one should first eat an olive's-worth in the place of Kiddush

paragraphs: Tzarik leekol bimqom haqqiddush lealtar; veim lo akal ad leachar zeman, lo yatza y"ch; abal im bedato haya leekol miyyad, veraq era lo ones venitakkeb leachar zeman, hare zeh yatza y"ch. mihu, yesh choleqim gam al zeh usebira lehu - apillu im haya bedato techilla leekol achar zeman, apillu achar shaa ushettayim, vaapillu achar shiur ikkul, name yatza bediabad; vekevan dqy"l sb"l, laken bekol gavna lo yachazor viqaddesh; mihu, im era zeh beqiddush hallayla, az qodem sheyyebarek "hammotzi" yeharher birkat haqqiddush, o yomar otah bepiv belo shem umalkut; veim hu beyom, yekavven bebirkat "hammotzi" lemitzvat qiddush keadam shemmeqaddesh al happat, veyomar pesuqim shel qiddush hayyom qodem nt"y.

clarification.explanation: One must eat in the place of Kiddush immediately after reciting it, and if he delayed and did not eat until some time had passed, he has not fulfilled his obligation. But if he intended to eat immediately and was only prevented by circumstances beyond his control that delayed him, he has fulfilled his obligation. There are lenient opinions that hold that even if he planned from the outset to eat only after some time — even an hour or two, and even after the time it takes to digest — he has fulfilled his obligation after the fact. Since there is a rule that we are lenient in cases of doubt concerning blessings, in any such case he should not go back and recite Kiddush again. Nevertheless, if this happened at the Kiddush of the night, before reciting the blessing of "Who brings forth bread" he should have the blessing of Kiddush in mind, or say it quietly without mentioning God's name; and if it is by day, he should have the commandment of Kiddush in mind during the blessing of "Who brings forth bread," as one who recites Kiddush over bread, and recite the verses of the sanctification of the day before washing his hands.
takeaways: One must eat immediately after Kiddush; if he delayed intentionally, he has not fulfilled his obligation
If he was prevented by circumstances beyond his control and delayed, he has fulfilled his obligation
Out of doubt, one does not recite Kiddush again, but should have the blessing in mind

paragraphs: Yakol adam leqaddesh laacherim "p sheeno okel immahem, veen bazeh chashash mishshum "qiddush shello bimqom seuda", kevan delahashshomeim hayyotzeim y"ch hu meqom seuda; umihu, kol heka shehamqaddesh eno okel, dehu atzmo eno yotze y"ch qiddush, o shekkebar qiddesh leatzmo bimqom seuddato veeno meqaddesh poh ella letzorek acherim davqa, h"z lo yeqaddesh laacherim lekattechilla, "k hem enam yodeim leqaddesh beatzmam.

Veim ellu haacherim shemmeqaddesh lahem enam yodeim lebarek birkat haqqiddush, ak birkat "bore peri haggapen" yodeim lebarek nistappeq harab "chesed laalapim" za"l im yakol lebarek lahem gam "bph"g"; vekatab demistabbera echad omer kol haqqiddush, laken yoter tob sheyyishteh sham rebiit; y"sh. vekatabti bs"d bsh"q "mqbtzl": im kebar qiddesh bebeto veakal uba leqaddesh leellu - day lo sheyyitam min hayyayin; veim lo qiddesh adayin - asur lo litom mizzeh hayyayin, kevan sheeno okel sham vekaasher niktob leqamman. veim yishteh rebiit km"sh harab "chs"l", h"z shanuy bemachloqet kaasher niktob leqamman; mihu, leqamman nebaer sheyyesh lismok al sebarat hammattirin lishtot rebiit leet hatztzorek; ulepi zeh banniddon didan name chashib tzorek, veshappir hora harab za"l lebarek "bph"g" g"k velishtot rebiit. vekol zeh hu, im kesheholek lebeto leqaddesh veleekol, sham nimtzaim banayv ubene beto shehu motzi otam y"ch qiddush immo, ak im bebeto lo yesh adam acher sheyyotziu y"ch qiddush, ella sham meqaddesh leatzmo bilbad, hinneh bazeh chozer venitqal besela hammachaloqet, kevan deyesh soberim im qiddesh bemaqom acher veshata rebiit yayin, yatza y"ch "qiddush bimqom seuda", veal ken, adam kazeh shehu meqaddesh aach"k bebeto leatzmo bilbad lo yaknis atzmo bedabar zeh leqaddesh laacherim techilla al semak sheyyishteh rebiit sham; vekol zeh hu beqiddush hallayla deikka birkat qiddush, abal beyom delekka birkat qiddush, let lan bah, veyukal leqaddesh laacherim techilla, vibarek "bph"g" veyishteh rebiit, veaach"k yelek lebeto viqaddesh apillu leatzmo bilbad, kevan deeno mebarek ella raq "bph"g".

clarification.explanation: A person may recite Kiddush on behalf of others in order to exempt them from their obligation even though he himself does not eat with them, and there is no deficiency of "Kiddush not in the place of a meal," since the listeners who are exempted are in the place of their own meal. However, when the one reciting it does not eat there, or has already recited Kiddush for himself in the place of his own meal and is reciting it here only for the sake of others, he should not, as the primary practice, recite it for them unless they do not know how to recite Kiddush themselves. If those others do not know how to recite the blessing of Kiddush but do know how to recite "Who creates the fruit of the vine" themselves, Rabbi Ḥesed LeAlafim raised the question of whether the one reciting Kiddush may recite that blessing for them as well (so that one person says the whole Kiddush), and he wrote that it seems preferable that he say the whole Kiddush himself, and therefore it is better that he drink a quarter-log of the wine there — and this counts for him as "Kiddush in the place of a meal" specifically when he afterward goes home, where his household is, and he exempts them together with himself in reciting Kiddush there. But if there is no one else at home for him to exempt, and he is going to recite Kiddush there only for himself, he again enters into the doubt of the dispute as to whether drinking a quarter-log elsewhere counts as "Kiddush in the place of a meal," and therefore such a person should not bring himself to recite Kiddush for others relying on the fact that he will drink a quarter-log there. All this concerns the Kiddush of the night, which has its own blessing; but by day, when there is no blessing of Kiddush, the matter is easier, and he may recite Kiddush for others first, recite "Who creates the fruit of the vine," and drink a quarter-log, and afterward go home and recite Kiddush even for himself alone.
takeaways: One may recite Kiddush for others even without eating with them, since they are in the place of their own meal
As the primary practice, one should do this only if they do not know how to recite Kiddush themselves
If he later returns home to recite Kiddush for himself alone without household members present, he should not rely on the quarter-log he already drank elsewhere, since this is disputed
The daytime Kiddush is easier, since it has no special blessing of Kiddush

paragraphs: Im meqaddesh laacherim veeno okel immahem vehu adayin lo qiddesh bebeto, hare zeh lo yitam kelum min hakkos, ki asur litom qodem qiddush shehu eno yotze y"ch beqiddush zeh, deen qiddush ella bimqom seuda.

clarification.explanation: One who recites Kiddush on behalf of others and does not eat with them, and has not yet recited Kiddush for himself at home, is forbidden to taste anything at all from the cup of wine, since it is forbidden to taste before Kiddush, and he himself does not fulfill his obligation with this Kiddush, as it is not in the place of his own meal.
takeaways: One who recites Kiddush for others not in the place of his own meal should not taste from the cup
The reason: he himself has not fulfilled his obligation with this Kiddush, and it is forbidden to taste before Kiddush

paragraphs: "p sheamarnu: en qiddush ella bimqom seuda, m"m, im akal kazzayit pat o kazzayit mine mezonot, o shata rebiit yayin millebad kos haqqiddush, yatza y"ch qiddush kan, veyakol leekol aach"k bemaqom acher belo qiddush; mihu, shear perot umashqin la mehanne. v"g dy" desaggi bishtiyyat kos haqqiddush beatzmo im yishteh mimmennu rebiit, m"m en lismok al sebara zo ella leet hatztzorek, kegon kos shel mila veen sham qatan lehashqoto; upoh irenu bagdad y" hamminhag pashut shehammohel mebarek al kos hammila veshoteh mimmennu rebiit, v"p sheomedim sham kamma qetannim, veen notenim leqatan lishtot; al ken tzarik shehammohel yitkavven latzet bazeh y"ch qiddush veyishteh rebiit shelema.

clarification.explanation: Even though we said "there is no Kiddush except in the place of a meal," if he ate, in the place of Kiddush, an olive's-worth of bread or of grain foods, or drank a quarter-log of wine in addition to the cup of Kiddush, he has fulfilled his obligation of Kiddush there, and may afterward eat his meal elsewhere without having to recite Kiddush again. Other fruits and beverages do not suffice for this. Some say it is enough to drink a quarter-log from the cup of Kiddush itself, but one should not rely on this opinion except in a time of need, such as the cup used at a circumcision when there is no infant there to give it to drink. In Baghdad the custom is that the mohel recites the blessing over the cup of the circumcision and drinks a quarter-log from it, and therefore he must intend thereby to fulfill his obligation of Kiddush and drink a full quarter-log.
takeaways: Eating an olive's-worth of bread or grain foods, or drinking an additional quarter-log of wine, fulfills the obligation, and one may then eat elsewhere
Other fruits and beverages do not suffice for this
Drinking a quarter-log from the cup of Kiddush itself suffices only in a time of need

paragraphs: Im shama qiddush mishkeno, yatza y"ch, kevan dehashshomea hu shomea bimqom seuddato, veraq tzarik sheyyitkavven hammiqdash lehotzio y"ch.

clarification.explanation: One who heard Kiddush from the mouth of his neighbor has fulfilled his obligation, since the listener is in the place of his own meal. The condition for this is that the one reciting Kiddush intend to exempt the listener from his obligation.
takeaways: One can fulfill the obligation by hearing Kiddush from a neighbor
Condition: the listener is in the place of his own meal and the one reciting Kiddush intends to exempt him

paragraphs: Yesh omerim deen meqaddeshin ella bimqom ner; veyesh omerim sheen haqqiddush taluy banner, vetzarik lehizzaher kisbara harishona leqaddesh bimqom ner, ki ken rauy lihyot "p hassod, veraq bishbil tzorek vehekreach gadol yesh lismok al sebara hashsheniyya.

clarification.explanation: Some say that Kiddush may be recited only in a place where there is a lit candle, and some say that Kiddush does not depend on a candle. It is fitting to be careful, as per the first opinion, to recite Kiddush in a place with a candle, for so it is proper according to the esoteric tradition, and only for a great need and necessity may one rely on the second opinion.
takeaways: It is fitting to recite Kiddush in a place with a lit candle, so it is proper according to the esoteric tradition
Only in a case of great necessity may one recite Kiddush without a candle

paragraphs: M" min hattora leqaddesh bidbarim, shenneemar: "zakor et yom hashshabbat leqaddesho" - zakerehu zekirot shabbat veqiddush. vetzarik lezakero biknisato beqiddush ubitziato behabdala; vy" shehabdala middibre soperim, veen tzarik min hattora ella biknisato, velaken min hattora yotze adam yede choba bitpillat arbit shel shabbat, veraq chaza"l tiqqenu leqaddesh al hayyayin; mihu, yesh omerim: kol sheyyesh lo yayin, eno yotze min hattora y"ch qiddush bitpilla; gam yesh omerim: kol sheeno mekavven bitpilla latzet y"ch qiddush, eno yotze min hattora.

clarification.explanation: It is a positive commandment from the Torah to sanctify the Sabbath with words, as it is said, "Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it" — to remember the Sabbath and sanctify it. One must remember it upon its entrance with Kiddush and upon its departure with Havdalah. Some say that Havdalah is a matter of the Sages, and that from the Torah it suffices to remember it upon entrance alone; accordingly, from the Torah a person already fulfills his obligation with the Sabbath evening prayer, and it was the Sages who enacted the recitation of Kiddush over wine. However, some say that one who has wine does not fulfill the Torah obligation of Kiddush through prayer, and some say that one who does not have the intention in his prayer to fulfill the obligation of Kiddush does not fulfill it from the Torah.
takeaways: Kiddush is a positive Torah commandment from the verse "Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it"
The Sages enacted that Kiddush be recited over wine
According to some opinions, one who has wine, or did not have the intention in prayer, does not fulfill the Torah obligation through prayer

paragraphs: Haqqiddush byv"t middibre soperim, vp"k yesh lo din qiddush shabbat lekol dabar. vegam hannashim chayyabin beqiddush shabbat min hattora veqiddush yv"t middibre soperim, diktib: "zakur" v"shamur" - kol sheyyeshno bishmira, yeshno bizkira (berakot k:).

clarification.explanation: The Kiddush of a festival is a matter of the Sages, yet in every respect it has the law of the Sabbath Kiddush. Women, too, are obligated in Kiddush — in the Sabbath Kiddush from the Torah and in the festival Kiddush by rabbinic law. Although women are generally exempt from time-bound positive commandments, they are obligated in Kiddush, because it is said "Remember" and "Observe," and whoever is commanded regarding the observance of the Sabbath is also commanded regarding its remembrance; and women are commanded regarding observance, and therefore also regarding remembrance.
takeaways: Festival Kiddush is a rabbinic matter, but has the law of any Kiddush
Women are obligated in Sabbath Kiddush from the Torah
The reason: "Remember and Observe" — whoever is included in observance is included in remembrance

paragraphs: Qatan, apillu hu ben y"g shana veyom echad, kol sheyyesh lehistappeq bo shemma lo hebi shette searot, eno motzi lo et haish velo et haishsha: veap al gab dehitpallelu haish o haishsha tepillat arbit, eno motziam y"ch, vkm"sh bs"d bsh"q "mqbtzl"; veayyen "tosepet shabbat", si' r, sq"g; v"eshel abraham", resh si' r v"mishbetzot zahab" sham; v"eliyya rabba", si' rg, s"q yb; "sh.

clarification.explanation: A minor, even one who has reached the age of thirteen years and one day, if there is doubt as to whether he has developed the signs of physical maturity (two pubic hairs), cannot exempt either a man or a woman from their obligation, since there is no certainty that he is an adult obligated in the commandments. And even if the man or woman had already recited the evening prayer, the minor does not exempt them from the obligation of Kiddush.
takeaways: A minor about whom there is doubt whether he has developed signs of maturity cannot exempt others from their obligation
This ruling holds even if the listeners had already recited the evening prayer

paragraphs: Ap al gab deqayma lan: qiddush shabbat deorayeta - muttar lekattechilla lehitpallel uleqaddesh mibbeod yom, desamekinan lahalaka keman deamar tosepet shabbat deorayeta; v"g deikka haramba"m udeimmeh dipligi - kebar hebi "mg"" za"l, si' rs"z, sq"g beshem ha"mareddekay" za"l, degam lemaen deamar tosepet shabbat derabbanan, yotze beqiddush zeh, kevan dibshaa dimqaddesh yabo aach"k lide chiyyub deorayeta; "sh. v"g dh"mg"" za"l hitzrik iyyun bazeh, veod, dehaggaon r" za"l katab, demiddibre mera"n "kesep mishneh" za"l meboar dela kh"mareddekay" za"l; "sh. veayyen od m"sh bs"d bsh"q "rab-berakot", dap l"d, veod m"sh bs"d sham bemaareket hap' bedin happidyon; y"sh; m"m ha ikka bazeh sepeq-sepeqa, vehu mithappek gam ken; veal ken nahagu haolam bazeh bekamma meqomot leqaddesh mibbeod yom, vehammachmir leqaddesh bevadday layla tabo alayv beraka, ak hammachmir leqaddesh bevadday layla, lo yitpallel mibbeod yom veyamtin harbeh ad layla vadday leqaddesh, dilkattechilla tzarik leqaddesh miyyad achar hattepilla vknz"l, ella yaaseh keminhag rabbenu haari"y za"l, leqabbel shabbat keshechamma berosh ilanot, deaz, ad sheyyitpallel arbit veyabo mibbet-hakkeneset veyomar happesuqim vehappiyyut vehazzohar shennohagim lomar qodem, yihyeh zeman chasheka viqaddesh.

clarification.explanation: Even though Sabbath Kiddush is a Torah matter, it is permitted as the primary practice to pray the evening prayer and recite Kiddush while it is still day — that is, before nightfall — since we rely on the opinion that the extension of the Sabbath is a Torah matter, and when one accepts the Sabbath upon himself while it is still day, the obligation of Kiddush applies to him. Although there are those who disagree, there is a doubt within a doubt that tips the scale toward leniency, and therefore the practice in many places has been to recite Kiddush while it is still day. One who is stringent to recite Kiddush only at certain nightfall — blessing will come upon him; but if he is stringent in this way he should not pray while it is still day and then wait a long time until night, since as the primary practice one must recite Kiddush immediately after the prayer. Rather, he should follow the custom of the Ari, who received the Sabbath when the sun was at the tops of the trees, so that by the time he finishes the evening prayer, returns from the synagogue, and recites the verses, the liturgical poems, and the passage from the Zohar customarily recited beforehand, it will already be the time of darkness, and he can then recite Kiddush.
takeaways: It is permitted to recite Kiddush while it is still day, based on the law of the extension of the Sabbath
One who is stringent to recite Kiddush only at certain nightfall — blessing will come upon him
One who is stringent should not pray while it is still day, but should follow the Ari's custom of receiving the Sabbath when the sun is at the tops of the trees

paragraphs: Qatan shehigdil venaasa ben y"g shana veyom echad belel shabbat qodesh - heeleti bs"d bsh"q "rab berakot", dap ld, deyamtin beqiddush ad layla vadday; y"sh; veken rauy lehorot bedin zeh lekattechilla, deen bazeh lo tircha velo hepsed, demah yapsid im yamtin ad hallayla? vehinneh vadday desamekinan achazaqa lechumera, lomar shehebi shette searot, dedavqa lehaqel la samekinan achazaqa bemidi deorayeta.

clarification.explanation: A minor who comes of age and becomes thirteen years and one day old on the very night of the Sabbath — it is fitting that he wait to recite Kiddush until certain nightfall (the emergence of the stars). This is how it is fitting to rule as the primary practice, since there is no trouble or loss in this — what would he lose by waiting until night? This is because we rely on the presumption to be stringent and say that he has already developed the signs of maturity and is obligated in the commandments from the Torah, and in a matter of Torah law we do not rely on presumption to be lenient.
takeaways: A boy who becomes bar mitzvah on the night of the Sabbath should wait to recite Kiddush until certain nightfall
The reason: there is no trouble or loss in waiting, and in a Torah matter one is stringent

paragraphs: Tzarik shebbene habbayit hashshomein qiddush min bh"b yasimu libbam heteb lishmoa birkat haqqiddush mittechilla vead sop. umi sheazenayv kebedot veeno yakol lishmoa, o shebbaal-habbayit zaqen umegamgem bilshono v" lahem leqaddesh bp" mikkamma sibbot hekrechiyyut, heeleti bsh"q "mqbtzl" shezzeh haadam sheeno yakol lishmoa habberaka min bh"b, yitten enayv bekos shebbeyad bh"b shemmeqaddesh alayv, veyomar belachash birkat haqqiddush kullah beshaa shbh"b meqaddesh; vesham hebeti dibre haggaon r" za"l bitshuba, si' z', sheasa tiqqun, lomar birkat haqqiddush beli peticha vachatima, upiqpaqti bazeh; y"sh. vesamakti bedabar zeh shekkatabti al m"sh harab "brk"y" za"l, si' rtz"h, avvat d', beshem mahari"y zayin za"l. ubeniddon didan chashib diabad, kevan d" lo leqaddesh al hakkos bp" uleachazu beyado.

clarification.explanation: The members of the household who hear Kiddush from the master of the house must pay close attention to hear the blessing of Kiddush from its beginning to its end. One whose ears are heavy and cannot hear, or whose master of the house is elderly and stammers so that he cannot be heard properly, and who cannot recite Kiddush himself for unavoidable reasons — this person who cannot hear should fix his eyes on the cup in the hand of the master of the house, and recite quietly the entire blessing of Kiddush while the master of the house is reciting it. This situation is considered as after the fact, since he is unable to recite Kiddush over his own cup and hold it in his hand.
takeaways: Listeners must hear the blessing from beginning to end
One who cannot hear should fix his eyes on the cup and recite the blessing quietly along with the one reciting Kiddush
This is a solution after the fact, for one who cannot recite Kiddush himself

paragraphs: Suma yukal leqaddesh ulehotzi ishto ubene beto yede chobat qiddush, dekol happoseqim chalequ al rabbenu yerucham bedin hassuma; mihu, im yesh piqqechim omedim al hashshulchan, vehassuma baal-habbayit la anina datah im yeqaddesh echad mibbene beto, tob sheyyeqaddesh zeh happiqqeach, latzet yede choba lekulle alema, kevan deepshar behaki.

clarification.explanation: A blind person can recite Kiddush and exempt his wife and household from their obligation, since all the halachic authorities disagree with Rabbeinu Yeruḥam, who was stringent regarding a blind person. Nevertheless, if there are sighted people at the table, and the blind master of the house does not insist that he himself recite Kiddush, it is good that the sighted person recite Kiddush, in order to fulfill the obligation according to all opinions, since this is possible.
takeaways: A blind person recites Kiddush and exempts his household
If there is a sighted person at the table and the master of the house does not insist, it is preferable that the sighted person recite Kiddush to satisfy all opinions

paragraphs: Asur litom apillu mayim qodem qiddush, mishshehiggia zeman haqqiddush dehaynu ben hashshemashot, apillu shello hitpallelu arbit adayin; mihu, im hu betaanit, muttar lehaddicha piv qodem qiddush. vehaaleti bsh"q "mqbtzl": kol shello nireh adayin shemesh apillu al kotel gabohha, nechshab lesapeq, veasur litom apillu mayim. upoh irenu bagdad y" matchil ben-hashshemashot shiba deqim qodem qeriat ha"mogerab" sheqqore besop sheat y"b, velaken poh irenu, kevan denishar shiba daqqim liqriat ha"mivgrab" lo yishteh apillu mayim, dechal alayv chobat qiddush, vkm"sh bsh"q "rab pealim" bitshuba, bs"d.

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to taste anything, even water, before Kiddush, from the moment the time of Kiddush arrives — that is, from twilight — even if one has not yet prayed the evening prayer. One who is fasting is permitted to rinse his mouth with water before Kiddush. As long as sunlight is still visible, even on a high wall, this is considered a doubt, and it is forbidden to taste even water. In Baghdad, twilight begins seven minutes before the call to prayer, which is at the end of the twelfth hour, and therefore once only seven minutes remain until the call, one should not drink even water, since the obligation of Kiddush has already applied to him.
takeaways: From twilight it is forbidden to taste even water before Kiddush
One who is fasting may rinse his mouth
As long as sunlight is still visible, even on a high wall — it is a doubt, and tasting is forbidden

paragraphs: Qiddush hallayla eno taluy bitpillat arbit, sheim yirtzeh leqabbel shabbat mibbeod yom uleqaddesh veleekol ulehitpallel arbit ballayla, rashshay, veraq tzarik sheyyatchil leekol chatzi shaa qodem zeman qeriat-shema; abal qiddush hayyom taluy bitpilla, dekol zeman shello hitpallel shacharit, lo chal alayv chobat qiddush; velaken, beyom shabbat babboqer yukal lishtot mayim qodem tepilla, mippene shekkevan shello hitpallel, lo chal alayv chobat qiddush. vekol zeh hu baanashim dechal alehem chiyyub tepilla babboqer achar ammud hashshachar, abal hannashim, mishsheala ammud hashshachar chal alehem chobat qiddush, vaasurin lishtot mayim qodem qiddush; mippene deyesh omerim: hannashim qayemi addina deorayeta, sheen lahem nussach qabua velo zeman qabua litpilla, ubepaam echad bayyom sheyyomru nosach tepilla, yatzeu yede choba, veim ken ledidehu, en haqqiddush taluy bitpilla, ulepikak, mishsheala ammud hashshachar asurin litom mayim qodem qiddush, vkm"sh harab "chesed leabraham" bitshuba, b"ch, si' va"v; y"sh.

clarification.explanation: The Kiddush of the night does not depend on the evening prayer: one who wishes to accept the Sabbath while it is still day, recite Kiddush, eat, and pray the evening prayer afterward at night, may do so, provided that he begins eating half an hour before the time for reciting the Shema. But the daytime Kiddush does depend on the prayer: as long as one has not prayed the morning prayer, the obligation of Kiddush has not applied to him, and therefore on Sabbath morning he is permitted to drink water before the prayer. All this applies to men, who are obligated in a fixed prayer in the morning. But women — from the moment dawn rises the obligation of Kiddush already applies to them, and they are forbidden to drink water before Kiddush, since some say that women are obligated in prayer from the Torah without a fixed text and without a fixed time, and it suffices for them to say some request once a day, so that for them Kiddush does not depend on prayer at all.
takeaways: The Kiddush of the night does not depend on prayer; the daytime Kiddush depends on the morning prayer
Men are permitted to drink water on Sabbath morning before they have prayed
Women are forbidden to drink water from dawn before Kiddush

paragraphs: Im shakach veakal qodem qiddush, apillu akal seuda gemura tzarik leqaddesh miyyad beet shennizkar, veasur lo litom kelum mishshennizkar ad sheyyeqaddesh. veim neenas o hezid velo qiddesh ballayla, yesh lo tashlumin lemachar kol hayyom, veyomar kol birkat haqqiddush shel layla chutz mipparashat "vaykullu" sheeno omerah bayyom. veim gam bayyom shakach o neenas velo qiddesh, venizkar ben hashshemashot shel hayyom shehu sapeq qodesh sapeq chol – hinneh, im hitpallel tepilla shel shabbat, hen ballayla, hen bayyom, nimtza yatza yede chobat qiddush min hattora, veraq nishar alayv chiyyub qiddush midderabbanan, vekevan dehu ben hashshemashot shehu sapeq yom, sapeq layla, heeleti bsh"q "mqbtzl", sheyyeqaddesh veyomar birkat qiddush shel layla beli shem umalkut, ella yeharher shem umalkut belibbo. vekatabti sham, deen lomar: lo nechayyeb oto leqaddesh kelal, kevan dehu sepeqa derabbanan veqayma lan, sapeqa derabbanan lequlla zeh eno, deha ikka disbira lehu: kol sheyyesh lo yayin, eno yotze y"ch qiddush min hattora bitpilla; veod, hinneh harab "tosepet-shabbat" katab: kol shello kivven latzet y"ch qiddush bitpilla, eno yotze y"ch min hattora, velaken tzarik leqaddesh al hayyayin, vibarek birkat haqqiddush belo shem umalkut. veim lo hitpallel shum tepilla beshabbat, nimtza hu chayyab beqiddush min hattora lekulle alema, veatta beben hashshemashot tzarik leqaddesh al hayyayin, vibarek birkat haqqiddush beshem umalkut, kedin birkat hammazon shehi min hattora, deim nistappeq bah, dechozer umebarek. veayyen leharab "mishbetzot-zahab" za"l, si' r", s"q y"; y"sh.

clarification.explanation: One who forgot and ate before Kiddush, even if he ate a full meal, must recite Kiddush immediately when he remembers, and it is forbidden for him to taste anything from the moment he remembers until he recites Kiddush. One who did not recite Kiddush at night, whether because he was prevented by circumstances or deliberately, may make it up the next day, throughout the entire day, and should recite the entire blessing of the night's Kiddush except for the passage of "Vayekhulu," which is not recited by day. If he also forgot or was prevented during the day and did not recite Kiddush, and remembered at the twilight at the close of the Sabbath, which is a doubtful time between holy and profane — if he had already prayed a Sabbath prayer (at night or by day) and thereby fulfilled the Torah obligation of Kiddush, with only a rabbinic obligation remaining, he should recite Kiddush and say the blessing without mentioning God's name aloud, but rather have God's name in mind in his heart. But if he did not pray any prayer at all on the Sabbath, he is obligated in Kiddush from the Torah, and therefore at twilight he should recite Kiddush over the wine and say the blessing with God's name and sovereignty, like the law of Grace After Meals, which is a Torah matter, where one who is in doubt about it goes back and recites the blessing again.
takeaways: One who forgot and ate before Kiddush should recite it immediately upon remembering
One who did not recite Kiddush at night may make it up the next day, without "Vayekhulu"
One who remembers at the twilight at the close of the Sabbath: it depends whether he had prayed — if so, without God's name and sovereignty; if not, with God's name and sovereignty

paragraphs: Tzarik sheyyihyeh al hashshulchan mappa tachat happat umappa lemala mishshene teamim: ha' zeker lamman, vehab' detayte seudeta deshabbeta biqara; veod yesh taam shelishi bemappa haelyona mishshum boshet happat.

clarification.explanation: There should be a cloth on the table beneath the bread, and another cloth above it, for several reasons: the first, in remembrance of the manna, which fell in the wilderness surrounded by dew both above and below; the second, so that the Sabbath meal be brought with honor; and there is a third reason for the upper cloth — out of honor for the bread, so that it not be "shamed," so to speak, when the blessing is recited over the wine before it.
takeaways: A cloth is placed beneath the bread and a cloth above it
The reasons: remembrance of the manna, honor of the Sabbath meal, and honor of the bread

paragraphs: Kos haqqiddush, apillu im hu naqi, tzarik haddacha mibbipnim ushetipa mibbachutz, umale al kol gedotayv, velo yihyeh pagum, sheim shata mimmennu – pegamo. veyihyeh shalem bispato ubebasis shello; vesedeq, apillu belo chissaron, posel. vetzarik sheyyitten oto adam acher bishte yadayv, vezeh hammiqdash yeqabbelennu mimmennu bishte yadayv betzad semolo keneged hechazeh, veachar-kak yochaz bo beyad yamin bilbad, veyagbihennu meal hashshulchan tepach lepachot, veyitten enayv bo shello yassicha dato mimmennu.

clarification.explanation: The cup of Kiddush, even if it is clean, requires rinsing on the inside and on the outside, and must be filled to its brim. It must not be blemished — that is, that people have already drunk from it, since drinking from it blemishes it. The cup must be whole in its rim and its base, and a crack invalidates it even if nothing is actually missing. Another person must hand the cup to the one reciting Kiddush with both hands, and he should receive it with both hands at his left side opposite his chest, and afterward hold it with his right hand alone, raise it at least a handbreadth above the table, and fix his eyes on it so that his mind does not wander from it.
takeaways: The cup requires rinsing inside and out, must be full to the brim, and must not be blemished
It must be whole, without a crack, in its rim and base
The manner of holding it: receive it with both hands, hold it with the right hand, raise it a handbreadth, and fix one's eyes on it

paragraphs: Im en lo ella kos yayin echad, meqaddesh bo ballayla, veshopek mimmennu lekos acher veshoteh; sheim yishteh min hakkos atzmo, hare zeh naasa pagum, veeno yakol leqaddesh al hannishar lemachar, lekak shopek mimmennu lekos sheni veshoteh mikkos hashsheni, vehannishar bekos rishon, yosip alayv mayim lemachar viqaddesh alayv. veim lo nishar ella meat, sheim yosip alayv mayim lehashlimo lirbiit lo yishshaer bo taam yayin shello yukal lebarek alayv "bore peri haggapen", hare zeh shotehu kullo ballayla. bammeh debarim amurim? im yesh lo kos acher lehabdala, abal im en lo kos acher lehabdala, hare zeh mannicha kos zeh lehabdala, viqaddesh ballayla ubayyom al happat, mippene deqiddush epshar leqaddesh al happat, abal habdala lo epshar. veayyen "eliyya raba", s"q k"g, v"tosepet shabbat", s"q k"t, ushear acharonim.

clarification.explanation: If he has only one cup of wine, he recites Kiddush over it at night, and before drinking he pours some of it into another cup and drinks from the second one. The reason: if he drinks from the cup itself it becomes blemished, and he will not be able to recite Kiddush over what remains in it the next day; therefore he pours a little into a second cup and drinks from there, and to what remains in the first cup he adds water the next day and recites Kiddush over it. If only a little remains in the cup, such that adding water up to a quarter-log would leave no taste of wine for the blessing of "Who creates the fruit of the vine," he should drink all of it at night. All this applies when he has another cup for Havdalah; but if he has no other cup for Havdalah, he should leave this cup for Havdalah, and recite Kiddush at night and by day over bread, since Kiddush can be recited over bread but Havdalah cannot.
takeaways: A single cup of wine: pour some into another cup and drink from it, saving the rest for the next Kiddush with added water
If too little remains, drink it all at night
If there is no other cup for Havdalah, save the wine for Havdalah and recite Kiddush over bread

paragraphs: Lekattechilla tzarik sheyyitam hamqaddesh male logemayv; umetzuvveh min hammubchar lishtot rebiit; ubediabad, im lo taam hamqaddesh vetaam echad min hamsubbin male logemayv, yatzeu kullam yede choba; umetzuvveh min hammubchar sheyyitamu kullam. bazzeman hazzeh en nimnaim millishtot mikkos sheshshata mimmennu chabero mechashash choli, meachar debarur lahem ki baal-habbayit sheqqiddesh veshata min hakkos, hu naqi veen bo choli.

clarification.explanation: As the primary practice, the one reciting Kiddush must taste a full mouthful of the wine (the amount that fills one cheek), and it is the most preferable fulfillment of the commandment to drink a quarter-log. After the fact, if the one reciting Kiddush did not taste it and one of those at the table tasted a full mouthful, they have all fulfilled their obligation, though it is the most preferable fulfillment of the commandment that they all taste it. Nowadays people are not deterred from drinking from a cup that another has drunk from out of concern for illness, since it is clear that the master of the house who recited Kiddush and drank from the cup is clean and free of illness.
takeaways: The one reciting Kiddush tastes a full mouthful, and it is preferable to drink a quarter-log
After the fact, it suffices that one of those at the table tasted a full mouthful
There is no concern about drinking from the shared cup of the master of the house

paragraphs: Qiddesh veqodem shettaam nishpak hakkos, yabiu lo kos acher vibarek "bore peri haggapen", ak lo yebarek birkat haqqadosh shekkebar berak otah, veken hu haddin im hipsiq bedibbur shello mitztzareke hasseuda. vegam hamsubbin yizzaharu shello yapsiqu bedibbur qodem sheyyitam hammiqdash.

clarification.explanation: If he recited Kiddush and, before he tasted it, the cup spilled, they should bring him another cup and he should recite over it only the blessing of "Who creates the fruit of the vine," but he should not repeat the blessing of Kiddush itself, which he has already recited. The same law applies if he paused with speech unrelated to the needs of the meal between the blessing and the drinking. Those at the table, too, should be careful not to interrupt with speech before the one reciting Kiddush tastes the wine.
takeaways: If the cup spills before tasting, he recites only "Who creates the fruit of the vine" again, not the Kiddush itself
Those at the table should not interrupt with speech until the one reciting Kiddush tastes the wine

paragraphs: En meqaddeshim al yayin sherecho ra mechamat shennetanuhu bikli maus, "p derecho vetamo yayin shemmebarekim alayv "bore peri haggapen", mishshum "haqribehu na lepachtik veku'". veken name en meqaddeshim al yayin shennitgalla, ulekattechilla yizzaher apillu al gilluy shaa muetet, veraq bediabad en lehaqpid, abal im abar layla achat begilluy, nipsal leqiddush "p shello namar recho vetamo.

clarification.explanation: One does not recite Kiddush over wine that has a bad odor because it was placed in an unclean vessel, even though the wine itself has a good smell and taste and one recites the blessing of "Who creates the fruit of the vine" over it; this is because of the verse "Offer it now to your governor" — one should not offer to a commandment something one would not offer to a dignitary. Likewise, one does not recite Kiddush over wine that has been left uncovered (left open). As the primary practice one should be careful even about a brief period of being left uncovered, and after the fact one need not be strict about it; but if a full night passed while it was left uncovered, it becomes invalid for Kiddush even though its smell and taste have not changed.
takeaways: One does not recite Kiddush over wine with a bad odor from an unclean vessel, because of "Offer it now to your governor"
One does not recite Kiddush over wine that has been left uncovered
If a full night passed while it was uncovered, it becomes invalid even if its smell and taste have not changed

paragraphs: Yayin shettamo chometz, apillu recho yayin, en meqaddeshin alayv veen mebarekin alayv "bore peri haggapen"; abal im tamo yayin, apillu recho chometz, meqaddeshin alayv, detaama iqqar.

clarification.explanation: Wine that has the taste of vinegar, even if its smell is still that of wine, is not used for Kiddush, and one does not even recite the blessing of "Who creates the fruit of the vine" over it. But if its taste is that of wine, even if its smell is that of vinegar, one may recite Kiddush over it, since the taste is the determining factor.
takeaways: Wine that tastes like vinegar is invalid for Kiddush and even for the blessing over wine, even if it smells like wine
Wine that tastes like wine is valid, even if it smells like vinegar, since taste is the determining factor

paragraphs: Yayin sheosin mitztzimmuqin shehem anabim yebeshim, im haya yotze mehem lachluchit al yede derika qodem sheshshirum bemayim, muttar lishrotan bemayim lehotzi mehem yayin uleqaddesh alayv; veim lav, asur leqaddesh al zeh, vegam "bore peri haggapen" en lebarek alayv.

clarification.explanation: Wine made from raisins (dried grapes): if the raisins would produce moisture by pressing even before they were soaked in water, it is permitted to soak them in water to extract wine from them and recite Kiddush over it. But if the raisins were completely dry and would not produce moisture by pressing, it is forbidden to recite Kiddush over the wine that comes from them, and one does not even recite the blessing of "Who creates the fruit of the vine" over it.
takeaways: Raisin wine is valid only if the raisins would produce moisture by pressing before soaking
Completely dry raisins produce wine that is invalid even for the blessing over wine

paragraphs: Im en lo yen kelal, yeqaddesh al happat. uballayla kak yaaseh: yittol yadayv bishbil birkat "hammotzi", veyesheb bimqomo, veyomar "vaykullu" beod happat mekusseh, veaach"k yiglennu vibarek "hammotzi" veeno botzea, veyomar az birkat haqqiddush beod shette yadayv al happat, ubotzea veokel. vehattaam shetztzarik lehannicha yadayv al happat bebirkat haqqiddush hu: ki kemo shetztzarik leechoz kos haqqiddush beyado, ken atta shehu meqaddesh al happat, tzarik leechoz happat beyado; vehaya day mittaam zeh lehannicha yad achat bilbad, ak kevan detzarik lebarek birkat "hammotzi" ulehannicha bah shette yadayv al happat, en nakon lesalleq yado achat achar birkat "hammotzi" bishat birkat haqqiddush, ella yishshaaru shette yadayv ad sheggomer birkat qiddush ubotzea, vekannizkar baacharonim za"l. vekol zeh hu ballayla, deyesh hekker gadol leqiddush "y birkat haqqiddush; ak beyom deen bo beraka shel qiddush, lo yesh hekker leqiddush bebirkat "hammotzi", al ken, im yesh lo chamar medina kegon shekar temarim o shekar seorim vekayyotze, yittol yadayv veyiqqach kos "rebiit" mechammer medina, vibarek "shehakkol", veyishteh male logemayv, veaach"k yebarek "hammotzi"; sheim yaqdim birkat "hammotzi" eno nikkar shemmeqaddesh. veim en lo chamar medina, o sheyyesh chamar medina veeno yakol lishtot ki yazziq lo vei epshar lishtoto kelal mechamat qoshi chariputo, shezzeh eno melummad lishtot mizzeh kelal yebarek "hammotzi" bilbad, veyibtza veyokal, ak yomar qodem birkat "hammotzi" happesuqim vehappiyyut shennohagim lomar beqiddush hayyom.

clarification.explanation: If he has no wine at all, he recites Kiddush over bread. At night he should proceed as follows: wash his hands for the blessing of "Who brings forth bread," sit in his place, and say "Vayekhulu" while the bread is still covered; afterward uncover it and recite "Who brings forth bread" but not yet cut it, and recite the blessing of Kiddush while both his hands are still on the bread, and only then cut it and eat. The reason he places his hands on the bread during the blessing of Kiddush: just as one holds the cup of Kiddush in hand, so too when reciting Kiddush over bread one holds the bread in hand, and since he has already placed both hands on it for the blessing of "Who brings forth bread," it is not proper to remove one hand, but rather both should remain until the end of the Kiddush. All this applies at night, when there is a great distinguishing feature for Kiddush through its special blessing. But by day, when there is no special blessing of Kiddush, if he has an important local beverage such as date beer or barley beer, he should wash his hands, take a quarter-log cup of it, recite the blessing of "By whose word all things came to be" and drink a full mouthful, and only afterward recite "Who brings forth bread" — for if he recites "Who brings forth bread" first, it will not be recognizable that he is reciting Kiddush. And if he has no such local beverage, or has one but cannot drink it because of its harshness, he should recite "Who brings forth bread" alone, and cut the bread and eat, but should first say the customary verses of the daytime Kiddush.
takeaways: No wine — recite Kiddush over bread: say "Vayekhulu," recite "Who brings forth bread," and say the Kiddush with both hands on the bread
By day, Kiddush over a local intoxicating beverage precedes "Who brings forth bread," so that the Kiddush is recognizable
No such beverage, or unable to drink it — recite "Who brings forth bread" alone and say the verses of Kiddush beforehand

paragraphs: Zehu seder haqqiddush hamyussad "p dibre rabbenu haari"y za"l: achar tepillat arbit yikkanes lebeto, ukesheyyikkanes limqom hashshulchan yomar beqol ram ubesimcha yetera: "shabbat shalom"! vinashsheq yede abiv vide immo im hem bachayyim. aach"k yistakkel beor hanner asher bareku alayv, veyistakkel bishte nerot vikavven shehem, ' keneged "zakur" ve' keneged "shamur". gam yekavven shehem, echad behe" rishona veechad behe" acharona shebbeshem hvy"h; v"p shehidliqu z' nerot likbod shabbat, im kol zeh hu lo yistakkel ella raq bishtayim, vikavven behistakkeluto sheyyairu nerot haelyonim veaach"k yaamod bammaqom sheyyosheb bo etzel hashshulchan veyomar beqol ram: "da hi seudeta dachaqal tappuchin". veaach"k yaqqip et hashshulchan derek yamin, veyachazor veyaamod bammaqom sheamad bo qodem haqqapa. veaz beamedo sham, yiqqach beyado shette aguddot hadas, shehem, echad keneged "zakur" veechad keneged "shamur", veyochazem vichabberem yachad kederek gedilatan ben shette yadayv, vibarek alehem "atze besamim" veyaricha bahem. veachar sheyyaricha, az tekep umiyyad, beodam mechubbarim yachad ben shette yadayv, yomar bepiv: "zakor veshamor bedibbur echad neemru", vegam yomar gam ken pasuq zeh: "recha nichocha ishsha laAdonai", ki betebot ellu remuzim kol hakkavvanot shel birkat harecha. veaach"k yachzor lehaqqip hashshulchan paam shenit bishtiqa beod hahadas beyado, ak en meakkeb sheyyihyeh ben shette yadayv gam beet shemmaqqip, ella day leechoz beyad yamin bilbad; veim yishshaer achuz bishte yadayv, hinneh mah tob umah naim, denakon laasot ken. veachar sheasa hahaqqapa hashshenit bahadas vechazar laamod bimqomo harishon, yishshaer hahadas beyad yemino lechibbub metzuvveh, veyomar: "shalom alekem malake hashsharet veku'", veyomar "melek malke hammelakim", velo yomar "mimmelek veku'", vknz' besiddur rab yaabe"tz za"l; veayyen "kap-hachayyim". veaach"k yomar: "ki malakayv yetzavveh lak veku'", vikavven beshem yvh"k shehu bs"t pasuq zeh, ubeshem kl"k shehu ramuz beot kap shel tebat "ki" ubeotiyyot l"k mittebat "malakayv"; veaach"k "Adonai yishmar tzetka uboeka veku'", veaach"k beli hepseq yomar tekep pesuqim "eshet chayil veku'", vikavven shehem k"b pesuqim keneged k"b tzinnorot shel mala, shibat hazzot hem petuchim umereqim shepa uberaka mehabbereka haelyona merosh kol hakketarim. veaach"k yomar "atqinu seudeta veku'", "ahalla shem Adonai beshir veku'", "Adonai uzzi veku'", veaach"k pizmon "azammer bishbachin veku'", veaach"k "yehe raava veku'", veaach"k zohar, vayyaqhel: "yoma da mitattera veku'". veda, d"g derabbenu haari"y yasad pizmon "azzemer veku'" hannizkar, leomero betok hasseuda, im kol zeh pashut hamminhag bekol hammeqomot leamero qodem qiddush, vk"k rab yaabe"tz za"l; veayyen lehaggaon chida" za"l, si' qs"v, ot g'. uminhagenu lipamim kesheyyesh sibba lemaher haqqiddush, kegon bime haomer vekayyotze neemar pizmon hannaz' betok hasseuda.

Aach"k yatchil beseder haqqiddush shehu hakanat hammaaseh vahakanat haddibbur. veqodem siddur haqqiddush yomar nosach zeh: "lyqbh"v veku'", hinneh anachnu baim leqayyem m" deorayeta leqaddesh et hashshabbat uleqayyem m" derabbanan leqaddesh al hayyayin, kemo sheppereshu rz"l p': "zakor et yom hashshabbat leqaddesho" - zakerehu bidbarim hanneemarim al hayyayin, letaqqen shoresh metzuvveh zo bemaqom elyon. vahare anachnu mukanim lehamshik orot elyonim lachaqal tappuchin qaddishin al yede hakana besod hammaaseh vahakana besod haddibbur. vihi ratzon millepaneka Adonai v", sheyyaaleh lepaneka keillu kivvenu bekol hakkavvanot hareuyot lekavven besod hammaaseh ubesod haddibbur asher yasedu lanu abadeka chakme yisrael beseder haqqiddush shel shabbat, veyaaleh lepaneka qiddush zeh im qiddushe baneka hayyodeim umekavvenim kahogen, veyimmashek shepa uberaka rabba bekol haolamot haqqedoshim, umishsham yimmashek shepa rab lenapshenu ruchenu venishmatenu leabedka beemet velishmor et kol shabbetot qadeshka kol yeme chayyenu, bemachshaba vedibbur umaaseh, beyira veahaba vesimcha rabba, vahare anachnu mukanim leqabbel alenu mitzvat aseh shel hatteshuba kemo shekkatub: "veshabta ad Adonai eloheka veshamata beqolo". vihi noam Adonai elohenu alenu veku'.

Vihi ratzon millepaneka Adonai v" sheyyehe atta et ratzon lepaneka, veyimmashek lanu ulenapshotenu ulebanenu ubenotenu ulekol yisrael shepa shalom, toba uberaka, chayyim chen vachesed verachamim, al yede shenayim veesrim tzinnorot elyonim asher hem petuchim umereqim shepa uberaka mibbereka haelyona merosh kol hakketarim. vihi ratzon millepaneka Adonai Adonai v", shebbizkut mitzvat mezigat kos hayyayin shel haqqiddush bemayim, mi'lo y'dnu mi'berakkuteka, umi'osher m'tannot y'doyka, ubizkut yaaqob temimeka asher mitteq haggeburot bachasadim kakkatub: "vayyabe lo yayin vayyeshet" - daarammi lah mayya beyena, ken berachameka vachasadeka yitmattequ kol haggeburot vehaddinin, ugemalanu chasadim tobim.

Vihi ratzon millepaneka Adonai v", shebbizkut mitzvot habberaka shel qiddush shabbat al kos yayin male, yitmalleu otiyyot "kos" shehem ka"p va"v same"k, sheolim mispar "habberaka", veyihyu tzinnorot leqabbel lanu shepa habberaka min habbereka haelyona mimmeqor habberakot, veyitqayyem banu miqra shekkatub: "yetzav Adonai itteka et habberaka baasameka ubekol mishlach yadeka". veatta adonay Adonai, hoel na uberak et bet abadeka, umibberakkuteka yeborak bet abadeka leolam. yihyu leratzon veku'.

Aach"k tatchil bahakanat hammaaseh, vehu: ki beodeka omed bimqomeka teqabbel hakkos bishte yadeka meadam acher, asher gam hu yochazennu bishte yadayv veyimserehu leka, veatta taamid hakkos bishte yadeka keneged hechazeh shellak, vch"z tasir miyyad semoleka uteachazennu beyad yemineka bilbad, kede liklol hassemol beyamin. ubeseder hammaaseh hazzot yesh kavvanot amuqqot verazin illain, velaken lo techasser ellu perat qatan misseder zeh, vetikkavvan bekol sheyyesh sod baddabar. veachar shettochazennu beyamin bilbad, az timzog lematteqo bammayim; vetob sheoto adam shemmasar leka hakkos bishte yadayv, hu yaaseh hammeziga beyad yemino. vehammeziga, yaasenna g"p, dehaynu, beshalosh hapsaqot bz"z, velo yitten kol me hammeziga bepaam achat. vedabar zeh shel hammeziga shettihyeh bg"p, lo nizkar bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l, raq nimtza meporash beseper "meeber-yabboq", velo beer tamo shel dabar. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" bearti bs"d hattaam: ki meboar bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l - yimzog hayyayin lematteqo bemayim shehu shelosha shemot y"h dhhy"n, sheolin mispar tisha yvdy"n d"b s"g m"h, veken katab besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l. nimtza sod hammayim shemmozeg bo hayyayin hu shelosha peamim yu"d h"h hannizkar. venimtza lepi zeh – gabra rabba amar milleta demistabber tama, ubevadday kak hayeta qabbala beyado mimmequbbalim neemanim. lekak, kol adam yizzaher bazeh, vealayv tabo birkat tob. veachar hammeziga titten eneka bekos hayyayin vetistakkel bo, veyesh sod amoq vekavvana gedola behistakkelut zo. vekol adam pashut, day lo lekavven behistakkelut ayin yamin bachamishsha hvyv"t sheolin mispar "ayin", ubehistakkelut ayin semol - g"k bachamishsha hvyv"t, sheolim mispar "ayin", kazeh:

clarification.explanation:
This is the order of Kiddush established according to the Ari: after the evening prayer, upon entering his house, he says loudly and joyfully "Shabbat shalom," and kisses the hands of his father and mother if they are alive. Afterward he looks at the light of the candles, focusing on two of them corresponding to "Remember" and "Observe" and to the two letters heh in the Name of God; although seven candles were lit, he looks only at two. Afterward he says "This is the meal of the Holy Field of Apples," circles the table to the right, and returns to his place. He then takes two bundles of myrtle corresponding to "Remember" and "Observe," recites over them the blessing "Fragrant trees," and smells them, saying "Remember and Observe were said in a single utterance" and "A sweet savor, an offering by fire to the Lord." Afterward he circles the table again in silence with the myrtle in hand. Upon returning he says "Peace be upon you," the verse "For He will command His angels concerning you" — intending the holy Names alluded to in its letters — and "The Lord will guard your going out," and then, without pause, "A woman of valor" (twenty-two verses corresponding to the twenty-two supernal channels). Afterward he says "Prepare the meal," "I will praise the name of the Lord," "The Lord is my strength," the liturgical poem "I will sing with praises," "May it be Your will," and finally a passage from the Zohar, Vayak'hel. Although the Ari established the poem "Azamer" to be said during the meal, the widespread custom everywhere is to say it before Kiddush; only at times when there is reason to hasten Kiddush, such as the days of the Omer, is it said during the meal.
Afterward he begins the order of Kiddush itself, which is the preparation of action and the preparation of speech, first saying the formula "For the sake of the union" and requests for the drawing down of abundance and blessing through the twenty-two supernal channels, intending that in the merit of the commandment of diluting the wine of the Kiddush cup with water, the powers of judgment will be sweetened with kindness, just as our father Jacob sweetened judgment ("And he brought him wine and he drank" — that he mixed water into the wine), and that in the merit of the blessing of Kiddush over a full cup of wine, the letters of the word "kos" (cup — kaf, vav, samekh) will be filled, which equal in number "the blessing."
In the preparation of action, he receives the cup with both hands from another person, holds it opposite his chest, holds it with the right hand alone, and dilutes it with water — as explained by Rabbi Yosef Chaim in his book Makbetzal — in three separate pourings, corresponding to the three Names of God in the vocalization Yud-Heh of the letters "heh-heh" [i.e., heh, heh, yud], which equal in number nine yuds of the Names Ayin-Bet, Samekh-Gimel, and Mem-Heh. After the dilution he looks at the cup of wine, and there is a deep secret and great intention in this looking — that he should intend, with his right eye, the five Names of YHVH that equal the numerical value of "eye," and likewise with his left eye, five more Names of YHVH.
takeaways: The Ari's order for welcoming the Sabbath: "Shabbat shalom," looking at the candles, circling the table, the blessing over the myrtle, and the kabbalistic liturgical poems

"A woman of valor" — twenty-two verses corresponding to the twenty-two supernal channels; and in the verse "For He will command His angels concerning you" one intends the holy Names "YHV"Kh" and "Kal"Kh" alluded to in its letters
The preparation of action: receiving the cup with both hands, holding it with the right, and diluting it with water in three pourings corresponding to three Names of Yud-Heh
In looking at the cup of wine after the dilution, one intends five Names of YHVH in each eye, corresponding to the numerical value of "eye"

paragraphs: Uminhagenu lirot et hammetzach beyayin, ulekavven: "metzach", mispar "hatzlacha". vehinneh bazeh nishlema hakanat hammaaseh, venaasa hattiqqun vehamshakat haor lihyot lemalkut chaqal tappuchin qaddishin, shh"s he" acharona shebbeshem hvy"h, "y hakana zo shel hammaaseh.

Venishar atta hakana hashshenit shehi hakanat haddibbur. ki hamshakat haorot vehattiqqun hannaaseh besod haqqiddush el bechinat he" acharona hanniqret "chaqal tappuchin qaddishin", hu naaseh bishte hakanot shehem: haachat besod hammaaseh, vehab' besod haddibbur, deraq "y shette hakanot ellu davqa yeshullam hamshakat haorot vehattiqqun shetztzerikin anachnu lehamshik atta belel shabbat beqiddush shel seuda zo hanniqret "seudeta dachaqal tappuchin qaddishin".

Vezehu inyan hakana hashshenit shel haddibbur sheyyihyeh al yede amirat "vaykullu" ubirkat haqqiddush, shehu bechinat haddibbur. utechillat hakkol tomar: "mizmor ledavid, Adonai roi veku'" kullo, veaach"k tomar: "yom hashshishshi, vaykullu hashshamayim". veyesh kamma teamim "p hassod, mah shemmosipim b' tebot "yom hashshishshi" im "vaykullu". veaach"k tomar "saberi maranan", v"p sheatta meqaddesh lebaddeka veen acher omed immeka, g"k tzarik atta lomar "saberi maranan", sheyyesh bazeh sod vekavvana. veaach"k tomar birkat "bore peri haggapen", veaach"k nosach birkat haqqiddush sheyyesh bah l"h tebot davqa, veaach"k tesheb vetishteh kos hayyayin meyushshab. veda, ki ballayla, kol seder haqqiddush vehabberakot tzarik lihyot meummad "p hassod, ak m"sh al shetiyyat hayyayin shettihyeh meyushshab, "p shekken heid rabbenu hrch"v za"l al minhag rabbenu haari"y za"l shehaya yosheb veshotehu, vkn"z bas' "peri etz chayyim" en qepida bazeh "p hassod, ella zehu mehilkot derek eretz shel hasseuda. veayyen "eliyya raba", si' q", s"q k"g, m"sh beshem "haroqeach"; "sh. veayyen baggemara gittin, dap ', ammud : shelosha debarim mazziqin gupo shel adam, vechad minnayhu - shata meummad; ak haramba"m za"l bah' deot, p"d, lo zakar zeh; veepshar ds"l, ad daabid lekilhu bebat achat. veepshar, dehaolam sheen maqpidin al shetiyya meummad, hu mittaam zeh; vk"z, meachar sherainu eduto shel rabbenu hrch"v za"l al minhag rabbenu haari"y za"l bekak, tzerikin anu lehizzaher bazeh.

clarification.explanation: In our custom one also looks at the reflection of one's forehead in the wine, intending that "forehead" is numerically equivalent to "success." With this the preparation of action is completed. Afterward comes the preparation of speech: first he says the entire psalm "A psalm of David: the Lord is my shepherd," then "The sixth day, and the heavens were finished" (adding "the sixth day" for reasons of the esoteric tradition), then "Attend, gentlemen" — which even one reciting Kiddush alone still says, since there is an intention in this — then the blessing of "Who creates the fruit of the vine," and then the text of the Kiddush blessing itself, which has exactly thirty-five words. Afterward he sits and drinks the wine while seated. It should be known that the entire order of Kiddush and the blessings at night must be performed standing, according to the esoteric tradition, but the drinking of the wine is done seated — not for a reason of the esoteric tradition, but as a matter of proper table etiquette, and because of three things that are harmful to the body, among them drinking while standing. Since Rabbi Chaim Vital testified to this custom of the Ari, one must be careful about it.
takeaways: One also intends, in looking at one's forehead reflected in the wine, that "forehead" equals "success" numerically
The order of speech: "A psalm of David," "Vayekhulu," "Attend, gentlemen," the blessing over wine, and the Kiddush blessing (thirty-five words)
Kiddush and its blessings are said standing, but the wine is drunk while seated

paragraphs: Benussach "atqinu seudata" basseuda shel hallayla, lo yesayyem: "veattiqa qaddisha uzeer anpin ateyan lisada bahadah". veken hu haddin beshel shacharit umincha name, lo yomar hassiyyum hazzeh, v"g dekatub ken bekol hassiddurim, vk"k b"seper hakkavvanot" shessidder mhrsh"v za"l; im kol zeh, besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l vesiddur rab yaabe"tz lo nizkar hassiyyum hannizkar. vekatab li hrh"g mhr" manni nr"v, deulay sebira lehu, mah shennizkar b"seper hakkavvanot" hu min hammatiq, velaken hu eno omer hassiyyum hannizkar; ad kan leshono. vegam ana abada kak noheg vekak moreh larabbim, yaan diklal gadol yesh bekol maqom: sheb veal taaseh adip.

Gam beinyan haqqapot shel hashshulchan katab li harab hannizkar nr"v, deminhago hu - "p shello nimtza lo hadas, yaaseh shene haqqapot belo hadas, vehodeti lo bazeh, ki haqqapa hashshenit belo hadas, im lo toil, lo tazziq, meachar demaqqip bishtiqa.

clarification.explanation: In the formula of "Prepare the meal" said at the night meal, one should not conclude with "and the Holy Ancient One and the Small Face come to feast with it," and likewise at the meals of the morning and the afternoon this conclusion should not be said. Although it is written this way in all the prayer books and in the Sefer HaKavanot, it does not appear in the prayer books of the Rashash and of Rabbi Yaavetz, and some have written that this conclusion in the Sefer HaKavanot is perhaps an addition of the copyist. Rabbi Yosef Chaim's own practice, and what he instructs the public, is not to say this conclusion, based on the principle that it is preferable to sit and refrain from acting. Likewise regarding the circlings of the table: even if myrtle cannot be found, one should still perform two circlings without myrtle, since the second circling without myrtle, even if it does not help, does no harm, as it is done in silence.
takeaways: In the formula "Prepare the meal," one should not say the conclusion "and the Holy Ancient One, etc." at any of the Sabbath meals
The principle: it is preferable to sit and refrain from acting
If there is no myrtle, one still performs two circlings of the table without it, since it does no harm

paragraphs: Im chal yv"t beshabbat lo nitparesh bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l ek yaaseh beseder haqqiddush vehashshulchan, veraq besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l, bepesach shechal beshabbat, katab sheyyakin al hashshulchan y"b lechamim, ushear debarim lo nizkeru beperush. vaanachnu, minhagenu bebetenu keshechal yv"t beshabbat, lehaqqip b"p uleharicha kishar shabbatot, veomerim "shalom alekem" v"eshet chayil" v"vihe raava", umesadderim y"b lechamim kishar shabbatot. gam neemar "atqinu seudeta" v"azammar bishbachin", yaan ki matzinu sheyyesh chiyyub kepi hassod beshalosh seudot; vegam bs"t bemincha - "vaani tepillati veku'"; veraq im chal rishon shel pesach beshabbat, en minhagenu lomar pizmon "azammar bishbachin", abal naasa haqqapot vahadas. veen li taam maspiq bedabar zeh leshannot ben lel-pesach lishar lelot yv"t beinyan happizmon hannizkar. veken im chal yv"t shel rosh-hashshana beshabbat, en minhagenu lomar pizmon "azammar beshabechin", abal naaseh haqqapot vahadas, vehashshem yitbarek yair enenu betorato, amen, ken yehi ratzon.

clarification.explanation: When a festival falls on the Sabbath, the Ari did not explain how to act regarding the order of Kiddush and the table; only in the prayer book of the Rashash, regarding Passover falling on the Sabbath, is it written to prepare twelve loaves on the table. Rabbi Yosef Chaim's custom in his own house when a festival falls on the Sabbath is to circle the table twice and smell the myrtle as on other Sabbaths, to say "Peace be upon you," "A woman of valor," and "May it be Your will," and to arrange twelve loaves as usual. They also say "Prepare the meal" and "I will sing with praises," since there is an obligation, according to the esoteric tradition, regarding the three Sabbath meals. But if the first day of Passover falls on the Sabbath, it is not their custom to say the liturgical poem "I will sing with praises," although the circlings and myrtle are still performed, and Rabbi Yosef Chaim has no sufficient reason for this distinction. Likewise, when Rosh Hashanah falls on the Sabbath, it is not their custom to say "I will sing with praises," but the circlings and myrtle are performed.
takeaways: A festival that falls on the Sabbath: the custom is as on other Sabbaths — circlings, myrtle, liturgical poems, and twelve loaves
The first day of Passover falling on the Sabbath — "I will sing with praises" is not said, but the circlings and myrtle are still performed
The same applies when Rosh Hashanah falls on the Sabbath
